title: Indivisible Greater Portland holds rally to encourage midterm election voting

tea.why: Participants gathered to encourage early voting in the midterm elections and express opposition to Republican incumbent Senator Susan Collins.
tea.want: To mobilize voters to support Democratic candidates and secure a Democratic majority in the U.S. Senate.
tea.changed: Oct 17: Approximately 400 people gathered at Deering Oaks Park to hear from Democratic candidates and Senator Elizabeth Warren.

summary: On Saturday, October 17, 2026, approximately 400 people gathered at Deering Oaks Park in Portland, Maine, for a rally organized by Indivisible Greater Portland. The event, held as part of a national "No Kings" day, focused on encouraging early voting in the upcoming midterm elections. Speakers at the rally included Democratic gubernatorial candidate Hannah Pingree, U.S. Senate candidate Troy Jackson, and U.S. Senator Elizabeth Warren. The speakers addressed topics including healthcare, the war in Iran, heating oil costs, immigration, and abortion, while criticizing Senator Susan Collins and President Donald Trump. The rally, also described as a "Defeat Collins Rally," highlighted the competitive nature of the Senate race between Jackson and Collins, which is considered a key factor in determining control of the U.S. Senate.
demands: Vote early in the midterm elections
response: No official response reported in the sources.
